title: fix: explicit max_tokens defaults for OpenRouter reasoning models
author: gggff123
pr_body_excerpt:
- Sets a 64,000-token default ceiling for seven OpenRouter reasoning models.
- Prevents low provider defaults from consuming the response budget on reasoning before visible output.
- Keeps caller-provided `max_tokens` authoritative.
- Mirrors the existing explicit-default pattern used by Claude/Bedrock models.

Closes #13594

gist.headline: Reasoning gets room to bloom
gist.blurb: Seven OpenRouter reasoning models now get a 64,000-token ceiling by default. They can finish thinking without eating the entire reply before it reaches the garden gate.
gist.summary: Set an explicit 64,000-token default max_tokens ceiling for seven OpenRouter reasoning models, while preserving caller-supplied max_tokens values, so provider reasoning defaults leave room for visible output.
gist.impact: Users of these OpenRouter reasoning models get more complete visible responses by default, with custom max_tokens settings remaining fully authoritative.
gist.visual_concept: Polli tends seven labeled code-plants in a cozy model garden, each growing from a lime-green pot marked “64K.” A retro terminal shows a long reasoning vine curling neatly into a bright visible-response flower, representing reserved output room; Polli wears a tiny gardener hat and checks a max_tokens dial.
